title: streaming: robust lifecycle controls for client cancel/disconnect, reconnect/resume, and server timeouts (OpenAI-compat)
author: Ava Martinez
release_notes: Fix streaming lifecycle handling: correctly propagate client cancels, detect and clean up on TCP disconnects, allow reconnect/resume semantics for clients that reattach within a grace window, and add server-side stream timeouts to prevent stuck generations. Maintains OpenAI SSE compatibility for cancel/disconnect events.
description: Summary: This PR implements a robust lifecycle for streaming responses that handles three common failure/migration modes: (1) client-initiated cancel, (2) abrupt client disconnects, and (3) reconnect/resume semantics when a client reattaches. It also introduces server-side timeouts to ensure background generators do not remain active if the connection is lost. Motivation: production incidents (SUP-412) and long-standing flakiness in streaming integrations showed cases where generators remained alive after clients canceled or unexpectedly disconnected, causing resource leakage and increased token costs. This change reduces leakage, improves observed latency/cost under high churn, and keeps the OpenAI-compatible SSE semantics developers expect. Changes (high level): - Add explicit cancel token propagation from gateway -> runtime so client-cancel requests cause immediate generator cancellation. - Track per-stream connection state with an attachment ID and last-seen heartbeat to allow reconnect/resume within a configurable grace period (default 15s). - On TCP/HTTP disconnect, mark stream as detached and start a short detach grace timer; allow reattach if the same client provides the attachment ID and resume token. - Add server-side stream idle and max-duration timeouts to force cleanup of orphaned generators. - Preserve SSE and JSON chunk semantics used by the OpenAI compatibility layer: we emit the existing `data: [DONE]` semantics and send a `event: cancelled` marker when a client explicitly cancels. Implementation notes: - runtime/generator: introduce ctx-aware cancel handling and a CancelRegistry that maps stream IDs to cancel channels. The generator checks cancel state at top-of-loop to avoid producing partial tokens when canceled. - gateway/stream_handler.go: add AttachID negotiation header (X-Redwood-Attach-Id) and resume-token validation; on upgrade, the gateway wires the HTTP conn to the stream manager and forwards cancel events. - stream_manager: maintains an LRU of active streams with last_seen timestamps; on disconnect, the stream is put into detached state and a cleanup task is scheduled. - metrics: new streaming.cleanup_count, streaming.reconnect_success, streaming.cancel_propagation_latency. - openai-compat: ensure existing SSE events still emitted and add a new `event: cancelled` for explicit cancels; reconnect/resume is exposed via the same SSE endpoint with an Attach ID query param. Compatibility and rollout: - Default behavior preserves previous semantics for clients that do not use attachment/resume. - The new AttachID/resume path is opt-in via header/query param and feature-flag guarded; feature flag enabled for 25% of traffic initially. Testing: - Unit tests for CancelRegistry, stream state transitions, and timeout triggers. - Integration tests simulate TCP disconnects and reattaches (including race windows). - E2E tests with the Python SDK demonstrating resume behavior. Performance: a microbenchmark shows <2% P50 latency impact for happy path streaming and removes ~60-90% of generator leaks in simulated churn. Checklist: - [x] Add CancelRegistry and cancel propagation hooks - [x] Implement AttachID negotiation and resume validation - [x] Add server-side timeouts and cleanup tasks - [x] Update OpenAI-compat SSE events - [x] Unit/integration/e2e tests - [x] Metrics and dashboards - [x] Rollout plan (FF -> 25% -> 100%) Related: ENG-7881 (streaming stability), ENG-7903 (openai-compat resume), SUP-412 (customer incident).

Author (Ava Martinez): Addressed by switching to a CAS on the registry and added a test that simulates concurrent attaches.

changelog: streaming: implement cancel/disconnect/reconnect lifecycle controls; add server timeouts and OpenAI-compatible cancelled event; opt-in resume via AttachID (FF rollout).
notes: Rollout: feature flag enabled progressively; monitoring in place to watch streaming.cleanup_count and reconnect success rate. Operations: If regressions are observed, FF can be rolled back per runbook ENG-7903-RB.
example_usage: curl -N -H 'X-Redwood-Attach-Id: <uuid>' \n  'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?resume=true'  # client may reattach by passing same Attach ID and resume=true
impact_summary: Reduces orphaned generator leaks under client churn; adds minimal latency overhead for happy-path streaming while enabling resumable streams for better UX in unstable networks.
